Every asynchronous result is fenced before adoption.

An ambiguous createConditionNote protects the append from duplicate retry before commit can be proven; this accepted DEC-063 REHYDRATE_BEFORE_RETRY tradeoff can omit a non-authoritative note after a pre-commit transport failure, but does not fabricate Check-In completion.

feature: Check-In authority, discovery, foreground/background and ambiguity lifecycle
review_notes: Activation preserves state only for the exact auth generation/location/workflow owner; any boundary change invalidates sequence, clears pending intake and rediscovers. Clear purges transient state. Background converts dispatched intake and continuation mutation/reconciliation into truthful ambiguity and invalidates late results; recognizing/discovery are likewise fenced. Ambiguous intake must first rediscover canonical server state, and only a zero-result recovery check enables an explicit retry using the same pending request. Multiple recoverables require user selection. Exact-target entry hydrates only the requested current CHECKING_IN session.

review_notes: Returning-customer corrections are transient and cleared on identity/location/owner boundary, clear and start-new. Phone input is normalized by the shared Jordan contract. Intake submit reuses a pending ambiguous operation ID or creates a secure new ID, fails pre-dispatch if CSPRNG identity is unavailable, binds targetLocationId, and ignores stale async outcomes. Returning-vehicle detail correction waits for intake success and then uses the existing versioned correction command.

Definite intake rejection releases the pending operation so a later deliberate Continue gets a new ID; ambiguous intake cannot replay until authoritative discovery completes. Secure UUID failure is reported without leaking the underlying entropy error or dispatching POST.
